newsitem.title: USA: Cargill facility running after Greenpeace protest.
newsitem.headline: Cargill facility running after Greenpeace protest.

text.p: Cargill Inc said its grain loading facility in Reserve, La., was running normally despite a Greenpeace demonstration on Tuesday held in protest of the company's use of genetically-altered soybeans.

"Our operations at Reserve, La. were only shut down for one hour on November 19," Cargill spokeswoman Lori Johnson said. "It was basically a minor disruption and we chose to stop loading for that brief period for safety reasons so that the Greenpeace folks would not be injured."
Environmental group Greenpeace has launched a global campaign against the spread of genetically-modified foods which it says are untested and a potential environmental risk.
In a statement, Greenpeace claimed it stopped activities at a Cargill terminal about 60 miles from New Orleans and unfurled protest banners.
The terminal called Terre Haute, is Cargill's largest facility and handles about 350 million bushels of grains and oilseeds a year, Johnson said.
"It didn't last long," said a supervisor at Cargill's Terre Haute, La., elevator. "They were pretty peaceful."
Other Cargill facilities were not affected by the demonstration, workers there said.
"We haven't seen them (Greenpeace)," said a supervisor at Cargill's grain loading facility in Port Allen, La..

At the time of the protest, Cargill was loading two vessels on Tuesday. "Ironically one was a corn vessel and the other one was for corn and wheat. There were no soybeans on these vessels," Johnson said.
Johnson said the facility had incurred no damage and there were no injuries to Cargill personnel or the protesters.
"Five people were arrested on Tuesday. Their (Greenpeace) ship showed on the Mississippi about 1515 CST on November 19 and they left at about 1700 CST," Johnson said.
